DexArena documentation

Install the released benchmark, inspect replay-validated data, and train and evaluate dexterous policies.

From an environment to an auditable result

DexArena brings together 10 long-horizon tasks, 30 stage tasks and four end effectors. Each complete sequence has physically grounded success predicates; a stage measures one skill, while a long task preserves the scene across skill transitions. The released demonstrations and the manuscript results use Franka arms with Sharpa hands.

New to the benchmark? Follow the OpenCabinet tutorial from installation to a checkpoint evaluation. Use the task catalog for visual stage definitions and the Leaderboard for the unchanged manuscript scores and their evaluation protocol.

Access is gated; the download endpoint is public

Request access once on the Hugging Face dataset page, then run hf auth login. Access is granted automatically after the request. Model backbones such as Cosmos may require separate approval. Start with one dataset or checkpoint rather than downloading the whole Hub repository.

A practical reading order

  1. Install and confirm that import tasks registers the environments.
  2. Download and validate a stage dataset, preserving its integrity certificate and raw replay recordings.
  3. Render the policy cameras and train, or go straight to a released checkpoint.
  4. Evaluate with the checkpoint's observation contract and the declared horizon. Keep episode records before aggregating.
  5. Record provenance, then cite the benchmark and methods.

Three tracks, different questions

TrackEvaluation unitWhat it measures
Stage execution30 stages · 50 episodes per stageAn individual skill from its stage reset distribution.
Cross-scene transfer30 stages × 3 native kitchensThe same frozen policy across held-out backgrounds; report mean ± scene standard deviation.
Long-horizon composition10 complete tasks · 50 episodes per taskComplete-sequence success after one initial reset, with no resets between stages.

Code supports Sharpa, Wuji, XHand and Gripper, using <Task>-<Hand>-v1 IDs. This does not imply published scores or datasets for every hand. The live registry is listed in Task table ↗.

Older website task descriptions and checkpoint directories can retain manuscript-era environment names. For executable commands, resolve the current release ID in the public task table; do not rename a checkpoint package to infer its controller binding.

Release notes are not new benchmark scores

These guides incorporate the maintainers' 9 November 2026 release-validation notes and the current public source interfaces. Timings, sizes and short functional runs are examples from a single workstation, not performance guarantees or replacement leaderboard results. The website does not run simulator, training or evaluation jobs in your browser.

Record your code commit, dataset revision and checkpoint hash. A source update can change fingerprints or interfaces; use the release's documented lineage handling instead of bypassing validation. For current code details, begin with Getting started ↗.
